chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in Ihram who has scabies that harms him. He said: 'He may scratch it. And if blood flows from it, there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does blood flowing from scratching scabies invalidate Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that scratching scabies while in Ihram is permissible, and crucially, that if the act causes bleeding, it does not invalidate the state of consecration or incur a penalty (kaffarah). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing harm (darar) without imposing undue burden, distinguishing between minor bodily functions like bleeding from scratching and the more significant prohibitions that break Ihram.
